page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor with a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced performance across most workloads. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core performance falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance for both small and large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth is relatively weak, falling in the bottom 25%. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. Text generation for small language models is a notable strength, registering in the top 25%, whereas medium model inference speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g7a.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power without resource contention. This instance is well-suited for applications such as web serving, application servers, medium-sized databases, software development compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks.

The x86_64 architecture includes 8 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not bundle local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution and small-model text generation, alongside average multi-core, memory read, and database operation speeds, though large-block memory write bandwidth is weak. The balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it a cost-efficient choice for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, application hosting, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
